title: Neurological assessment

sources.use: Glasgow Coma Scale structured-approach website and assessment aid (copyright (c) Teasdale and Jennett, RED)

objectives: Use the same structured approach and stimuli each time.
Record components and rating terms, not just a number.
Account for sedation, intubation and injury, and escalate change immediately.

items.text: Stimulate in a stepped way and only as much as needed; use finger-tip pressure before trapezius or supraorbital pressure; avoid repeated painful stimulation beyond what is needed.
Record the components and rating terms, not just a number; record non-testable with the reason; compare with previous assessments; report change immediately.
Account for sedation, analgesia, paralytics, intubation and injuries and record doses and timing so the team can interpret findings.
Interpretation bands and management decisions belong to the medical team; follow unit policy.
Component definitions and scoring are not reproduced (copyright); use the unit-approved scale and training.
Use the same structured approach and stimuli each time to allow comparison.
Report change promptly and document the escalation.
Communicate with relatives honestly and avoid predictions.
Record components, stimuli used, confounders and escalation per your unit's documentation standard.

checklist.text: Note sedation, analgesia, paralytics, intubation and injuries that affect testing.
Use the same structured stepped approach and stimuli each time.
Record each component and its rating term, not just a total.
Report change immediately and document who was told.
Record non-testable items with the reason.

gaps: Interpretation bands, ICP/CPP management and brain-injury guidelines: not covered.
GCS component wording: copyright; permission required to reproduce.
